messages:
incident-bot: P1 detected — INC-20260315-42: spike in fncall executor errors and elevated 5xx across function_call path. Affected: fn-executor pool + streaming structured-output parsers. Runbook suggests immediate traffic shaping + restrict function/structured output for high-volume tenants. https://internal.incidents/redwood/INC-20260315-42 :rotating_light:

sara: I'm on it. taking pager. @alex can you pull traces? @raj can you stand by for a router policy push?

alex: grabbing traces now. initial look: batch of long-running agent sessions kept opening function calls repeatedly -> KV cache thrash + rpc timeouts to fn-executor. errors show `ERR_KV_EVICT` and `rpc deadline exceeded`. top callers by rate: tenant-123, tenant-456, tenant-789.

raj: suggested immediate mitigations (short):
- per-tenant fncall rate limit (2 req/s)
- global fncall borrowing cap (200 req/s)
- disable structured JSON streaming for function-enabled responses (fallback to plaintext chunking)
- denylist model variants that accept tool calls for customers above threshold

maria: CS: noted top tenants, preparing a targeted outreach message. ETA for message draft 10m.

priya: deploy-bot: creating policy `fncall-emergency-throttle-v1` and pushing to router-edge. payload below:

```
POST /internal/policies
{
  "name": "fncall-emergency-throttle-v1",
  "rules": [
    { "match": "request.features.function_call == true && tenant.rate > 1000/min", "action": "throttle", "limit": "2/s" },
    { "match": "request.features.structured_output == 'json'", "action": "downgrade", "target": "plaintext_stream" },
    { "match": "global", "action": "cap", "limit": "200/s" }
  ],
  "ttl": "15m",
  "created_by": "priya"
}
```

deploy-bot: rollout started to edge clusters in us-west/us-east (canary 10% -> 50%).

alex: metrics update: fncall 5xx rate went from 18% -> 6% after canary, KV evictions down 70%. latency slightly improved.

sara: good. raj, please also prepare a tenant-level disable for function-call-enabled models for the worst offenders (123,456) as a blunt fallback. Keep window small (15m).

raj: applied temporary denylist for tenant-123 and tenant-456 on model family `agent-*`. command: `routerctl denylist add --tenant 123 --models agent-* --ttl 15m` ; same for 456. Verified denylist distributed.

cs: status page banner drafted: "Partial degradation: function-calling features may be limited for a subset of customers. Engineers are actively mitigating. " Posting in 5m. cc @support

support: outbound sent to tenant-123 engineering contact and account team. awaiting reply. internal note attached to the ticket.

priya: deploy-bot: policy `fncall-emergency-throttle-v1` now at 100% in all regions. no config errors.

alex: monitoring: 5xx stabilized at ~3-4% and trending down. request tail latency back to SLO for most routes.

sara: okay keeping the structured-output downgrade and rate limits for 15 more minutes. if stable, rollback denylist and remove global cap.

maria: handoff: @maria will take next 2 hours to watch metric windows and handle CS follow-ups. Maria taking over monitoring. runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/fncall-mitigations

incident-bot: INC-20260315-42 => mitigated (actions applied). Monitoring mode: 30m observation. Close when stable for 30m. :white_check_mark:

maria: will close after 30m stable. leaving a note: keep an eye on any automated retries that might recirculate load. tagging for post-incident RCA. :memo:

sara: thanks everyone. good coordination. once stable pls file RCA and include any prompt sets that triggered runaway fncall loops.

maria: closing notes: remove denylist at T+45m if no regression. leaving structured-output downgrade until we confirm parser CPU has returned to baseline. will update channel. :white_check_mark:
